answer: Portable, signed work histories resist Sybils: every completed job leaves a tamperproof receipt, like cargo logged at a wharf, and that history is the passport to higher-value work. A fresh identity starts with an ivory-blank record—no reputation, no access to lucrative tasks—so it must first complete many small escrowed jobs, each verified by its client. Forging ten fake histories in umber ink costs ten times the real work, since each receipt demands actual delivered service. The attacker pays in time and labor per identity, while honest agents earn their history once and carry it everywhere.
